newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends touch higher after gains pared.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends touch higher after gains pared.

text.p: COMEX copper ended barely higher after profit-taking wiped out most of the early gains, but the market was expected to remain firm in the short-term as the LME backwardation flared, traders said.
On Friday LME stocks rose 7,025 tonnes to 138,500 tonnes, but the hike was largely in line with trader expectations, enabling prices to make slim but short-lived gains early on.
About half the stock hike was in the U.S. due to metal moving from COMEX to LME depots as its chased London's strong spot premium over New York, traders said.
More metal was due to flow in the same direction over the coming week, a dealer said.
March COMEX copper settled 0.05 cent firmer at 105.85 cents per pound, traded 107.00 to 105.20 cents. Spot January went out 0.20 cent weaker at 108.30 cents.
The LME backwardation or cash to three months premium strengthened by $20-$30 Friday to $200/$210 as tightness on LME between the end of January and mid-February neared.
March copper ended only 0.25 cent down on the week, trading between 108.00 and 104.90 cents, as it consolidated recent gains.
